  [1] File: .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml (line ~2006)
      Problem: strong_edit_claim_regex excludes verbs that edit_claim_regex treats as edits (modif*, change*). The edit_claim_regex includes:; - `modif(y|ied|ies)` and `change(d|s)?`; But strong_edit_claim_regex only has:; - `update(d|s)?` `add(ed|s)?` `remove(d|s)?` etc. (no modif* or change*); When editor writes "Modified X; no changes required" in the "- none" first-line case (line ~20040), contradiction detection uses strong_edit_claim_regex which won't match "Modified" or "Changed", causing valid edit claims to be incorrectly filtered out as false-positive EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST. The remainder check uses edit_claim_regex correctly but the primary contradiction check uses the weaker strong_claim version.; ### Issue 2: Script missing edit_claim_regex entirely

      Problem: Lines: 2006-2007, 2011, 2045-2060; Inconsistent regex coverage between `edit_claim_regex` and `strong_edit_claim_regex` breaks mixed-claim detection.; The `strong_edit_claim_regex` (line 2007) is missing the `modif*` and `change*` verbs present in `edit_claim_regex` (line 2006) and `bullet_edit_regex` (line 2011). When the editor writes a line like "- Modified script; no changes required", the line matches the "no-change declaration" filter and is discarded. The mixed-claim recovery logic (lines 2045-2060) then fails to restore it because `strong_edit_claim_regex` does not recognize "Modified" as an edit verb. This leads to valid edit claims being ignored, potentially resulting in `EDITOR_CHANGES_LOST` false negatives (where the system thinks no changes were made despite the editor claiming them).
